findings.title: Spawned flusher processes are never killed/terminated
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py _ensure_processes_alive checks `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` before kill, and join does the same before terminate. Processes are created with `multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process` which is SpawnProcess, a sibling of the default ForkProcess exposed as multiprocessing.Process, not a subclass. The isinstance is therefore always False for real subprocesses, so hung processes are never killed and join never terminates them. On hang detection a new process is started for the same shards while the old hung process keeps running, causing duplicate flush/produce to buffered-segments, Redis contention, and leaked zombies.

findings.title: Join timeout break leaves remaining flusher processes unwaited
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py join loops over all flusher processes but does `if remaining_time <= 0: break` out of the for-loop. If the deadline expires while waiting for an early process, later processes are never waited on nor terminated, leaving background processes running after rebalance/shutdown. Old and new generations can then flush the same Redis shards concurrently and duplicate segments to Kafka.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag shard vs shards
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py the produce timer uses tags={"shard": shard_tag} while the wait_produce timer on the next line uses tags={"shards": shard_tag}. The pluralization mismatch splits what should be the same dimension, breaking dashboards/alerts grouped by shard and creating extra tag cardinality.

findings.title: Negative flusher_processes causes KeyError, zero silently ignored
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py `max_processes or len(...)` treats 0 as unset and `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(...))` accepts negatives. The --flusher-processes CLI option has no validation, so --flusher-processes=-1 makes num_processes negative, process_to_shards_map empty, and `i % num_processes` maps every shard to 0 which raises KeyError on startup. Zero does not mean zero processes but silently falls back to one-process-per-shard, opposite of user intent.

findings.title: Added flusher wait is no-op because sleep is mocked
findings.body: In tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py the test patches `time.sleep` to a no-op and then calls `time.sleep(0.1)` to give flusher threads time to process after advancing drift. Because sleep is mocked the wait does nothing, so join can set stopped before the background thread flushes. The test relies on a busy-loop race and will be flaky, not deterministically verifying the flush.
